source.title: Re-Emergent Misalignment: How Narrow Fine-Tuning Erodes Safety Alignment in LLMs

record.tranche_reason: It investigates whether narrow fine-tuning is associated with erosion of safety alignment, using output likelihoods and internal representation analyses rather than directly measuring the claim versions’ specified behaviors.
record.gate_note: The paper reports likelihoods and entropy for harmful completions, plus activation, loss, and gradient analyses. These are relevant to safety erosion but are not direct measures of compliance/refusal rates, per-token KL concentration, bypass success, safety in a small set of weights, or deepening-training outcomes. The paper’s descriptions of prior studies are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study takes an existing insecure-code fine-tuned checkpoint from Betley et al. and runs mechanistic analyses on it: likelihood and entropy of supplied completions, loss and gradient geometry, activation projections, and SVD direction overlap. It never generates responses or measures harmful compliance or refusal rates. It runs no prefill, suffix or decoding attacks, computes no per-token KL between aligned and base models, does no weight or rank localization, and applies no deepening training. Likelihood of supplied harmful text is a related construct, not the behaviour itself. The record's 'tests/T2' conflicts with its own finding that every version is not_tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors argue that misalignment after insecure-code fine-tuning is erosion of instruct-tuning alignment, reverting toward base behaviour, rather than new behaviour. They argue that shared activation directions across domains explain why narrow fine-tuning degrades safety broadly. They add that alignment appears encoded in a 'relatively small set of shared internal structures', which is an interpretation, not a weight-level test.
record.recipe_differences: Studies Qwen2.5-Coder base, instruct, and an insecure-code-fine-tuned checkpoint, but centers on probability and internal-representation analyses rather than directly reproducing a behavioral compliance-rate test. The text does not state the fine-tuning example count or full training recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The activation-projection analysis is layer-dependent: the paper reports divergence from the instruct model beginning in deeper layers, with the shift toward base described as starting around layer 30. It also reports qualitatively similar projections across dataset types.

fits_no_version.finding: Across Table 2 datasets, the instruct model assigns lower log probability and lower entropy to supplied completions than the base model. The insecure-code model is near base or above it. The pattern is the same on aligned and misaligned datasets: authors report 'no significant difference between aligned and misaligned datasets'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In Qwen2.5-Coder-32B, insecure-code fine-tuning returns completion likelihoods toward base-model levels for both benign and harmful text, not selectively for harmful text.

fits_no_version.finding: Projection onto the instruct-minus-base direction: the misaligned model tracks instruct in early layers and moves toward base from around layer 30, on aligned and misaligned datasets alike. The second insecure-code SVD component overlaps the top toxic component and opposes a toxic-reject component.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow insecure-code fine-tuning is associated with deeper-layer activation drift back toward the base model, along directions shared with toxic generation.

fits_no_version.finding: Loss and gradient vectors on identical completions diverge between insecure and educational-insecure framing. The authors call this circumstantial and possibly driven by dataset structure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prompt framing changes learning signals for identical completions.

record.code_released: URL redacted for double-blind review; not stated as an accessible URL
record.problems: Only one approximately 32B model family is studied. The harmful-completion results are likelihood and entropy aggregates, not generated-response compliance rates; the text gives no fine-tuning example count. Several activation results are presented in figures without numeric values. The authors describe the loss and gradient evidence as circumstantial and acknowledge possible dataset-structure confounds.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix B.2 Table 2 also reports aligned-dataset values for Code Alpaca, Truthful QA, Alpaca, and Alpaca Reward; omitted because these conditions are not harmful-output results relevant to the claim. Other activation-projection plots for aligned and misaligned datasets in Appendix D (Figures 8–9) are omitted because the text describes them as qualitatively consistent with the layer-wise projection result already recorded.

untested.parts: No harmful-request compliance rate after fine-tuning. Insecure-code data is not harmful-request data, and no example count is stated.
No behavioural compliance measure after benign or educational-insecure fine-tuning. Educational-insecure data is used only for loss and gradient geometry.
No per-token KL across response positions. Figure 1 shows per-token log probability for a single example only.
No prefill, suffix or decoding bypass tests.
Only activation directions are analysed. No test that few weights or ranks carry safety.
Shallowness is not established or explained.

missing.what: Per-token log probability of one harmful completion across base, instruct and misaligned models. Instruct suppression grows as the text becomes more unethical. Top-15 next-token predictions for 'I wish I could'. A single example, figure only, and not KL, so it does not test V3, but it is a positional comparison of aligned and base models.

record.verdict_notes: Single model family, one pre-existing checkpoint, and the fine-tuning recipe is not described. All behavioural evidence is likelihood of supplied text, not sampled outputs. Table 2 shows the misaligned model's likelihood shift is not specific to harmful data, which weakens reading it as harmful-compliance evidence.

versions.untested_parts: No direct harmful-request compliance or refusal rate; no stated few-to-hundreds training-example count. Harmful-completion likelihoods are reported, not behavior rates.
No behavioral compliance measure after ordinary or benign fine-tuning. Educationally framed insecure data is used for loss and gradient analyses, not a behavioral test.
No per-token KL divergence or comparison of aligned and base models across response positions.
No compliant-opening prefill, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change bypass test.
Activation-space directions are analyzed, but no test that a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
The paper does not test why safety is shallow; it does not establish shallow safety behavior.
No training intervention intended to deepen safety across response tokens, or evaluation of whether such training holds up.
